title: Finite evaluation of the completed reduction augmentation
statement: Let T be a scheme and d an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For any K in the unbounded derived category of completed-coefficient module sheaves and any n in the natural numbers (representing positive quotient exponent n+1), evaluate the canonical derived quotient augmentation [def-weil-pbc-reduction-augmentation] at n. Compose its source with the inverse canonical derived constant/evaluation isomorphism and its target with completedReductionEvaluation. The resulting arrow from K to the scalar-restricted n-th derived reduction is exactly the unit of the normalized derived scalar-extension/restriction adjunction [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower]. No completeness, boundedness, scheme Noetherianity or nonemptiness is required.

proof.text: On a K-flat complex P, postcompose the evaluated augmentation with exact scalar restriction of the invertible scalar computing counit, followed by its derived-localization factor. The defining completedReductionEvaluation normalization replaces that composite by evaluation of the tower computing counit. The augmentation normalization stratumUnit_formula replaces augmentation followed by this counit by the localization of the ordinary module quotient unit. Naturality of the evaluation factor and constantEvaluation_factors cancel the constant/evaluation comparison. Its degree-n ordinary component equals the scalar-extension unit by stratumModuleUnit_component. The normalized derived scalar adjunction gives the same morphism, proving equality after cancellation. This works also for the empty scheme, zero object and n=0 (the positive exponent-one quotient).

Express the evaluated augmentation as a natural transformation. Every complex admits a quasi-isomorphism from a K-flat complex. Exact localization inverts this quasi-isomorphism; naturality and essential surjectivity of Q extend equality to every derived object. The module also retains the existing generic finite unit, evaluation-transition, cocycle and pullback-transition calculations as proved private helpers for the parent, and proves its generic augmented-projection helper by the adjunction triangle, projection-counit normalization and constant/evaluation coherence.

For checking time, the module additionally retains the already-proved generic actual/intrinsic completion transport and its integral specialization as private helpers. These use the same augmentation-transport identity, normalized Koszul quotient comparison and reflector representative as the parent, with no changed data or statement.

lean.statement:
theorem sfCompletedReductionAugmentation_level_unit (T : Scheme.{u})
    (K : d.derived T) (n : ℕ) :
    (ringedConstantTowerEvaluation (reductionModules T (d.completedRing T)) (op n)).inv.app K ≫
      (reductionTowerDerivedEvaluation T (reductionModuleRing T (d.completedRing T)) n).map
        ((completedReductionAugmentation d T).app K) ≫
      (completedReductionEvaluation T d n).app K =
    (pbcDerivedScalarAdjunction (d.projection T n)).unit.app K
